visual_anchor: HRCT: basal subpleural reticulation, parenchymal bands, and/or honeycombing with pleural plaques; early disease may show subpleural dots/lines.
rationale: Strong exposure-linked fibrosis pattern. Keep distinct findings as a unified asbestos-related thoracic disease topic with pleural plaque and rounded-atelectasis subsections.

visual_anchor: CT shows bilateral pleural plaques, especially along posterolateral chest wall and diaphragmatic pleura; plaques may be calcified.
rationale: Highly imageable exposure effect, best grouped with asbestosis and rounded atelectasis in one asbestos-related thoracic disease topic.

visual_anchor: Pleural-based rounded mass adjacent to thickened pleura, with converging bronchovascular structures curving into the lesion (comet-tail sign).
rationale: Memorable mass mimic in asbestos-related pleural disease; include as a subsection in unified asbestos-related thoracic disease page.

visual_anchor: V/Q scan shows segmental mismatched perfusion defects; CTPA shows eccentric organized thrombus, webs/bands, pouch defects, mosaic perfusion, and enlarged bronchial arteries.
rationale: Distinct chronic organized vascular disease from acute PE, with treatable pulmonary hypertension and diagnostic imaging criteria.

visual_anchor: HRCT may show peripheral ground-glass opacity or consolidation; high-attenuation lung opacities and high-attenuation liver/spleen support iodine-rich drug accumulation.
rationale: Distinct medication-associated lung injury pattern with a potentially useful attenuation clue.

visual_anchor: CT after intravenous injection of crushed tablets may show centrilobular micronodules/tree-in-bud pattern, sometimes high attenuation, with upper-lobe/costophrenic sparing.
rationale: Distinct particulate exposure with memorable distribution and vascular/centrilobular imaging; separate from silicosis and coal pneumoconiosis.

visual_anchor: After long-bone injury, conjunctival/axillary petechiae; chest CT may show diffuse or patchy ground-glass opacity, septal thickening, and centrilobular nodules.
rationale: Time-sensitive trauma syndrome with a characteristic clinical petechial distribution plus pulmonary imaging findings.

visual_anchor: HRCT shows lower-lung-predominant ground-glass opacity or fine reticulation with relative subpleural sparing; traction bronchiectasis if fibrotic.
rationale: Subpleural sparing is a useful imaging pattern distinguishing NSIP from UIP, though secondary causes must be considered.

canonical_name: Alveolar Macrophage Pneumonia (formerly Desquamative Interstitial Pneumonia)
visual_anchor: HRCT typically shows diffuse/basal ground-glass opacity in a smoker, sometimes with subpleural sparing and emphysema.
rationale: Use current ERS/ATS 2025 term “alveolar macrophage pneumonia” (AMP); preserve DIP as a former-name synonym. Radiology and smoking context support a visual topic.

visual_anchor: HRCT shows upper-lobe centrilobular/paraseptal emphysema with lower-lobe subpleural fibrosis/honeycombing in the same patient.
rationale: Distinct mixed pattern with physiologic consequences and radiographic contrast across lung zones.

visual_anchor: Expiratory HRCT shows patchy lobular air trapping/mosaic attenuation, sometimes with bronchiectasis and bronchial-wall thickening.
rationale: Distinct small-airway disease and bilateral counterpart to the unilateral postinfectious Swyer–James pattern.

canonical_name: Diffuse Idiopathic Pulmonary Neuroendocrine Cell Hyperplasia (DIPNECH)
visual_anchor: HRCT shows diffuse mosaic attenuation/air trapping with multiple small centrilobular nodules and occasional tumorlets or carcinoids.
rationale: Distinct airway-neuroendocrine disorder with a recognizable combined CT pattern.

visual_anchor: Unilateral air trapping/hyperinflation or atelectasis on expiratory chest radiograph; object may be directly visualized at bronchoscopy.
rationale: Common, actionable pediatric airway emergency with clinical and endoscopic teaching value.

visual_anchor: Contrast CT shows loculated lenticular pleural fluid with enhancing visceral and parietal pleura (split-pleura sign); necessitans extends through chest wall.
rationale: Broaden existing thoracic empyema necessitans page to Pleural Empyema (including necessitans), preserving the existing sign and representing extension as a complication.

visual_anchor: Inspiratory/expiratory CT shows peripheral cystic bronchiectasis from deficient cartilaginous support in fourth- to sixth-order bronchi, with dynamic ballooning/collapse.
rationale: Rare congenital bronchiectasis phenotype; imageable but the classic description is based on limited cases.

visual_anchor: CT shows a blind-ending bronchus with a mucocele/bronchocele and adjacent segmental hyperinflation/air trapping.
rationale: Characteristic paired mucocele plus hyperinflation is highly teachable and distinct from other congenital lung malformations.

visual_anchor: Smooth, sharply marginated water-attenuation mediastinal (often subcarinal) or intrapulmonary cyst on CT; proteinaceous contents may increase attenuation.
rationale: Distinct foregut-derived mediastinal lesion and useful cystic-mass differential.

visual_anchor: CTA shows left pulmonary artery arising from right pulmonary artery and passing between trachea and esophagus, often with airway compression.
rationale: Distinct vascular-airway congenital anomaly with actionable cross-sectional anatomy.

visual_anchor: Axial CT/bronchoscopy shows a circular O-shaped trachea lacking the posterior membranous wall, often with long-segment stenosis.
rationale: Distinct congenital airway morphology; may accompany pulmonary artery sling but should remain an independently describable anomaly.

visual_anchor: HRCT shows geographic ground-glass opacity concentrated in the right middle lobe, lingula, and paramediastinal lung, with air trapping/hyperinflation.
rationale: Distinct infant diffuse-lung-disease pattern; diagnosis requires clinical context and careful exclusion of alternatives.

visual_anchor: Pediatric CT shows a unilateral multicystic or mixed solid-cystic lung mass; solid type may invade pleura/chest wall.
rationale: High-stakes pediatric malignancy and key differential for CPAM; separate organ-specific neoplasm.

visual_anchor: CT shows one or more peripheral, often slowly growing calcified nodules; cysts may coexist.
rationale: Distinct parenchymal amyloid manifestation from existing tracheobronchial amyloidosis; imaging rather than shared pathology justifies separate scope.

visual_anchor: CT shows a well-circumscribed or lobulated anterior mediastinal soft-tissue mass; pleural “drop” implants can indicate dissemination.
rationale: A common anterior mediastinal tumor with distinct thoracic anatomy and staging pattern.

visual_anchor: Anterior mediastinal mass with macroscopic fat, fluid, soft tissue, and coarse calcification/teeth; fat-fluid level may be present.
rationale: Highly recognizable imaging pattern of a mature mediastinal germ-cell tumor; retain distinct thoracic site from ovarian/testicular teratomas.

visual_anchor: Smoker with ill-defined upper-lobe centrilobular nodules, patchy ground-glass opacity, bronchial-wall thickening, and often emphysema on HRCT.
rationale: A distinct symptomatic smoking-related ILD with an imageable pattern, although it overlaps smoking-related macrophage disorders.

canonical_name: Hard-Metal Lung Disease (Giant Cell Interstitial Pneumonia)
visual_anchor: Occupational CT may show ground-glass opacity, centrilobular nodules, mosaic attenuation/air trapping, and fibrosis with traction bronchiectasis.
rationale: Distinct cobalt/tungsten exposure-associated ILD; imaging alone is nonspecific, so anchor to occupational history and giant-cell interstitial pneumonia.

visual_anchor: Chest CT commonly shows bilateral ground-glass opacity with subpleural/lobular sparing, sometimes consolidation or upper-lobe centrilobular nodules.
rationale: Current exposure-linked acute lung injury with a recognizable but nonspecific imaging spectrum; preserve exposure-based diagnostic framing.

visual_anchor: CT shows upper-lobe-predominant centrilobular ground-glass nodules or calcified nodules in chronic renal failure/hyperparathyroidism; bone scintigraphy may show diffuse pulmonary uptake.
rationale: A radiologically distinctive metabolic complication that is separate from primary alveolar microlithiasis.

visual_anchor: Occupational radiograph/CT may show numerous dense fine nodular opacities from retained iron-containing dust, often with little functional impairment.
rationale: One of three named inert-metal pneumoconioses; keep separate candidate records, but they may be presented together in an inert-metal pneumoconiosis section because clinical effects and imaging patterns overlap.

visual_anchor: Occupational radiograph/CT may show numerous dense fine nodular opacities from retained tin-containing dust, often with little functional impairment.
rationale: One of three named inert-metal pneumoconioses; keep separate candidate records, but they may be presented together in an inert-metal pneumoconiosis section because clinical effects and imaging patterns overlap.

visual_anchor: Occupational radiograph/CT may show numerous dense fine nodular opacities from retained barium-containing dust, often with little functional impairment.
rationale: One of three named inert-metal pneumoconioses; keep separate candidate records, but they may be presented together in an inert-metal pneumoconiosis section because clinical effects and imaging patterns overlap.

visual_anchor: Infant chest radiograph may show diffuse hazy/granular opacities; HRCT shows ground-glass opacity with septal thickening, and later-onset forms may develop cysts/fibrosis.
rationale: Separate gene-defined surfactant disorders have overlapping radiology, but disease-specific age/severity and syndromic context justify distinct records; avoid claiming imaging alone identifies the genotype.

visual_anchor: Infant chest radiograph may show diffuse hazy/granular opacities; HRCT shows ground-glass opacity with septal thickening, and later-onset forms may develop cysts/fibrosis.
rationale: Separate gene-defined surfactant disorders have overlapping radiology, but disease-specific age/severity and syndromic context justify distinct records; avoid claiming imaging alone identifies the genotype.

visual_anchor: Infant chest radiograph may show diffuse hazy/granular opacities; HRCT shows ground-glass opacity with septal thickening, and later-onset forms may develop cysts/fibrosis.
rationale: Separate gene-defined surfactant disorders have overlapping radiology, but disease-specific age/severity and syndromic context justify distinct records; avoid claiming imaging alone identifies the genotype.

visual_anchor: Infant chest radiograph may show diffuse hazy/granular opacities; HRCT shows ground-glass opacity with septal thickening, and later-onset forms may develop cysts/fibrosis.
rationale: Separate gene-defined surfactant disorders have overlapping radiology, but disease-specific age/severity and syndromic context justify distinct records; avoid claiming imaging alone identifies the genotype.

visual_anchor: Unilateral opaque small hemithorax with marked ipsilateral mediastinal shift, absent ipsilateral main bronchus and pulmonary vasculature, and compensatory contralateral hyperinflation.
rationale: Distinct congenital absence of lung, bronchus, and vessels; differentiate from aplasia and prior pneumonectomy.

visual_anchor: Unilateral volume loss and mediastinal shift with a blind-ending rudimentary main bronchus but absent distal parenchyma and pulmonary vessels on CT.
rationale: Distinct from agenesis by rudimentary blind bronchus; retain as separate congenital anomaly.

canonical_name: Proximal Interruption of a Pulmonary Artery
visual_anchor: CT angiography shows absent proximal branch pulmonary artery with distal intrapulmonary branches supplied by systemic collaterals and a small ipsilateral lung.
rationale: Distinct congenital vascular anomaly and cause of hemoptysis; not equivalent to scimitar syndrome.

visual_anchor: CTA/MRA shows focal pulmonary-vein narrowing or abrupt cutoff with regional septal thickening, ground-glass edema, waxing/waning opacities, or decreased perfusion.
rationale: Distinct venous obstruction and important mimic of infection or pulmonary embolism; congenital and acquired forms can be explained together.

visual_anchor: CTPA shows a lobulated, expansile filling defect with vessel enlargement/wall-eclipsing; MRI shows heterogeneous enhancement and PET may be FDG avid.
rationale: Rare but critical PE mimic with a distinct tumor-like vascular imaging pattern.

visual_anchor: Dynamic expiratory CT or bronchoscopy demonstrates excessive expiratory collapse of the trachea and/or main bronchi.
rationale: Distinct dynamic central-airway disorder; separate from tracheal diverticula/bronchiectasis in Mounier–Kuhn syndrome.

visual_anchor: Endoscopy/CT shows a short concentric scar-like narrowing below the glottis, commonly in the cricoid/subglottic airway.
rationale: Duplicate cross-specialty candidate with Otolaryngology; leave ADD for central deduplication into one airway page.

visual_anchor: CT shows smooth submucosal tracheal or main-bronchial wall thickening/narrowing, sometimes with longitudinal extension; bronchoscopy shows a submucosal lesion.
rationale: A tracheobronchial salivary-gland-type primary has a characteristic airway-centered appearance and is clinically distinct from conventional lung carcinoma and salivary-gland ACC; the existing broad primary lung carcinoma topic excludes subtype proliferation, so a focused airway topic is justified.

visual_anchor: Central endobronchial soft-tissue nodule/mass on CT causing focal airway narrowing, atelectasis, or recurrent postobstructive infection.
rationale: Distinct bronchial primary with airway-specific presentation; do not merge with oral/salivary mucoepidermoid carcinoma solely for shared histology.

visual_anchor: CT shows a solitary, well-circumscribed, often peripheral lung nodule/mass with variable enhancement or calcification.
rationale: Distinct mesenchymal lung neoplasm with imageable mass pattern; histology/genetics confirm.

visual_anchor: Usually a well-circumscribed, peripherally located, round/oval nodule with homogeneous enhancement; marginal pseudocapsule or overlying-vessel sign may appear.
rationale: Distinct lung neoplasm with useful solitary-nodule image, not a generic “sclerosing” tumor subtype.

visual_anchor: Well-circumscribed paravertebral/posterior mediastinal mass, often with smooth neural-foraminal widening or dumbbell extension on CT/MRI.
rationale: Thoracic anatomic location provides distinct imaging differential; do not merge solely with vestibular schwannoma.

visual_anchor: Smooth elevated intact hemidiaphragm with preserved continuity on CT/ultrasound; dynamic ultrasound can show reduced excursion.
rationale: Distinct from diaphragmatic hernia because the diaphragm remains intact; clear radiographic/dynamic anchor.

visual_anchor: Chest radiograph/CT shows mediastinal air outlining the heart, great vessels, or trachea, sometimes with continuous-diaphragm sign.
rationale: Distinct from pneumothorax and tension pneumothorax; clinical context distinguishes spontaneous from traumatic/iatrogenic causes.

visual_anchor: Neonatal imaging may show diffuse interstitial thickening, septal lines, ground-glass opacity, and pleural effusions; pathology demonstrates dilated lymphatics.
rationale: Distinct congenital diffuse lung disorder; do not collapse with diffuse pulmonary lymphangiomatosis, which is a separate entity.

canonical_name: Alveolar Capillary Dysplasia with Misalignment of Pulmonary Veins (ACD/MPV)
visual_anchor: Neonate with refractory pulmonary hypertension and diffuse bilateral opacities; imaging is nonspecific.
rationale: Pathology-led lethal developmental disorder without a disease-specific clinical or radiologic visual anchor; defer under current scope.

visual_anchor: CT may show multiple cysts and nodules, often peribronchovascular, with airway-wall thickening or calcification.
rationale: Distinct parenchymal/airway deposition disorder from systemic AL amyloidosis and tracheobronchial amyloidosis; radiologic pattern merits separate topic.

visual_anchor: Thin branching, bone-density opacities in dependent lower-lobe subpleural/interstitial lung on CT, often incidentally detected.
rationale: Distinct branching ossification pattern and useful radiologic teaching entity.

visual_anchor: Bronchoscopy shows black anthracotic pigmentation with bronchial narrowing/stenosis, often involving the right middle lobe; CT may show calcified nodes and atelectasis.
rationale: Highly recognizable bronchoscopic appearance with useful TB/exposure context.

visual_anchor: Multiple left pleural-based nodules on CT after remote splenic trauma/splenectomy; lesions enhance like splenic tissue and show uptake on heat-damaged RBC scan.
rationale: Distinct benign thoracic nodule mimic with a specific history and confirmatory nuclear medicine study.

visual_anchor: CT may show enlarged main pulmonary artery, right-heart enlargement, and peripheral vascular pruning; imaging supports but does not establish PAH.
rationale: Distinct clinical pulmonary vascular diagnosis with supportive imaging; right-heart catheterization is required for diagnosis.

visual_anchor: Imaging may show multifocal ground-glass opacity or consolidation resembling organizing pneumonia or diffuse alveolar damage.
rationale: Primarily a histopathologic pattern with no specific radiologic signature; parent instruction recommends deferring absent stronger visual value.

visual_anchor: CT findings can include centrilobular nodules, tree-in-bud opacities, septal thickening, and pulmonary artery enlargement, all nonspecific.
rationale: Severe but usually diagnosed pathologically or postmortem; no reliable disease-specific visual anchor for a standalone atlas topic.

visual_anchor: After aspiration of kerosene/fire-breathing fuel, CT may show fat-attenuation consolidation or crazy-paving with dependent distribution.
rationale: Named exposure syndrome is a form of exogenous lipoid pneumonia; merge into existing exogenous_lipoid_pneumonia and preserve “fire-eater” as context/synonym.

visual_anchor: Acute exposure may cause nonspecific bilateral opacities, delayed pulmonary edema, or bronchiolitis obliterans.
rationale: Toxic exposure syndrome with nonspecific radiology and no reliably distinctive photograph; defer per focused visual-atlas criteria.
